lesson.title: 5.9 I'd like a sandwich, please
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.goal: Order politely at a café with I'd like …, please. and understand the question What would you like?
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.9 Ordering Politely 1: At a Café: A1 orders with Can I have …, please? and hands things over with Here is your …; A1+ 5.9 orders with I'd like …, please. and understands the waiter's What would you like?, after 5.3's Would you like …? offer. I'd like is learnt as a whole (the short form of would is not taken apart). Each cast member stands at the café counter with what they ordered; the waiter is never pictured, so a narrator in a voice other than the customer's asks. Listen sets I'd like against A1's Can I have …? On 2026-11-23 the menu and the bill were added: a customer asks for the menu before ordering and for the bill after the meal.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.9 Can I have …, please?; A1+ 5.3 Would you like …?; A1 5.13 sandwich; A1 5.14 cup, of, cake; A1+ 4.15 some.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say I'd like as one word-group (IDE-like), with the d short; do not require native-like speed.
